name: Lumbar spine MRI
description: Shows disc herniations and narrowing that compress nerve roots. Guidelines reserve it for persistent symptoms in people who may be candidates for surgery or injection, or for severe or progressive neurological deficits.

name: Femoral stretch test (clinician)
description: Lying face down, the clinician bends your knee; reproduction of your usual thigh pain is positive.

accuracy.population: Spine-centre patients with radicular leg pain < 12 weeks

name: Knee-jerk (patellar) reflex (clinician)
description: A reduced knee-jerk on the painful side points toward an L3/L4 root.

accuracy.population: Spine-centre patients with radicular leg pain < 12 weeks

name: Ankle-jerk (Achilles) reflex (clinician)
description: A reduced ankle-jerk on the painful side points toward an S1 (or L5) root.

accuracy.population: Spine-centre patients with radicular leg pain < 12 weeks

name: Gait and balance examination: wide-based gait, Romberg test (clinician)
description: A clinician watches you walk and checks your balance with feet together and eyes closed.

accuracy.population: Specialty-clinic patients with low back pain

accuracy.locator: Table 3, 'Abnormal Romberg test result' (primary study: Katz 1995)
accuracy.population: Specialty-clinic patients with low back pain

name: Active piriformis test + seated piriformis stretch test (clinician)
description: Two examination maneuvers that load the piriformis region while the clinician feels for tenderness. Combined, they were the most accurate findings in the source study.

accuracy.locator: Abstract, Results (active piriformis + seated piriformis stretch combined)
accuracy.population: Posterior hip pain patients undergoing endoscopy

name: Nerve conduction / EMG, then MR neurography or ultrasound if unclear
description: Electrodiagnostic studies help confirm a nerve entrapment outside the spine; MR neurography, MRI or ultrasound clarify the cause when the diagnosis is still unclear.

name: Pelvic compression test (clinician)
description: A clinician performs the same compression test this tool guided you through, under standard conditions.

accuracy.population: Patients diagnosed with meralgia paresthetica, retrospective series

name: Diagnostic pudendal nerve block
description: Pain relief after an anaesthetic injection around the pudendal nerve is one of the five Nantes diagnostic criteria; expert consensus endorses these criteria for diagnosis.

name: Specialist assessment against the Nantes criteria
description: A pelvic pain specialist assesses you against the 4+1 Nantes criteria.

name: Superior cluneal nerve block
description: If pressing a point on the back of the pelvic rim about 7 cm from the midline reproduces your pain, a clinician can inject local anaesthetic there to test whether the superior cluneal nerve is the source.

name: Pudendal neurophysiology study + image-guided pudendal nerve block
description: Nerve conduction testing of the pudendal nerve combined with an image-guided anaesthetic injection; together they helped identify patients who improved after decompression surgery.

accuracy.population: Refractory pudendal entrapment patients; reference = improvement after surgery; no control group

name: Pelvic imaging: colour duplex ultrasound or MRI of the pudendal nerve
description: Imaging can show entrapment or rule out other causes; its role is still limited and figures come from patients already meeting the Nantes criteria.

accuracy.population: 96 consecutive patients evaluated for pudendal neuralgia; reference = neurological criteria

accuracy.locator: Results, MRI (primary study: Piloni et al.)
accuracy.population: 580 patients meeting Nantes criteria

name: Hip-knee flexion test (clinician)
description: An examination maneuver that was more specific for superior cluneal entrapment than for other causes of chronic low back pain.

accuracy.population: 200 patients with chronic mechanical low back pain; reference = US-guided SCN block

name: Needle EMG of the inner-thigh (adductor) muscles
description: In the source case series, needle EMG showed denervation of the adductor muscles in obturator entrapment.

name: Michel clinical score for piriformis syndrome (clinician)
description: A 12-point score combining history with piriformis stretch, resisted-contraction and palpation tests; 8 or more is 'probable'. It was derived against patients with disc-related nerve root compression, the main alternative.

accuracy.population: 250 cases vs 30 disc-root patients + 30 healthy controls (case-control; likely overestimates)

name: FAIR-position H-reflex study (electrodiagnostic)
description: Nerve testing that checks whether the H-reflex slows when the hip is held flexed, adducted and internally rotated. This is an electrodiagnostic test, not the bedside FAIR maneuver. Note: in a later study the FAIR-position delay did not significantly separate piriformis syndrome from disc-related root compression (0.7 vs 0.46 ms, p = 0.06; Michel 2013, Table 1). A systematic review notes the original study compared against people without symptoms rather than patients with other causes of sciatica, so it did not establish the test's accuracy (Hopayian 2010).

accuracy.population: 918 consecutive patients; reference = clinical working definition

name: MR-neurography-guided genitofemoral nerve block
description: A precisely targeted anaesthetic block of the genitofemoral nerve. In the source series, 88% (14/16) of patients with a positive block had a successful genitofemoral-targeted intervention, and 71% (5/7) with a negative block had a successful intervention on another target.

name: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve conduction study
description: Sensory nerve conduction is the standard electrodiagnostic test. Evoked potentials (SSEP) are a weaker fallback, mainly when conduction can't be recorded, e.g. in obesity.

accuracy.population: 120 patients with meralgia paresthetica
120 patients with meralgia paresthetica
21 meralgia patients vs 21 controls

name: MR neurography of the sciatic notch
description: Specialised MRI of the nerve. Piriformis asymmetry plus a bright (irritated) sciatic nerve at the sciatic notch separated piriformis syndrome from similar-looking sciatica. Caveat: cases were partly defined by response to a piriformis injection, which is a weak reference standard (Hopayian 2010).

accuracy.population: 239 consecutive patients with sciatica unexplained by standard work-up

name: Ultrasound measurement of piriformis thickness
description: A piriformis muscle thicker than about 1 cm on ultrasound was associated with piriformis syndrome (compared with healthy people, which overstates accuracy).

accuracy.population: 58 cases vs 58 healthy controls

name: EMG of the lower abdominal wall muscles
description: Electromyography detected abnormalities in some but not all confirmed cases, so a normal result doesn't rule it out.

accuracy.population: Definite ilioinguinal-iliohypogastric entrapment

name: Musculoskeletal ultrasound of the back of the pelvic rim
description: Ultrasound can show tissue changes around the superior cluneal nerves (fascial nodules, thickening, bony spurs). Pilot data only.

accuracy.locator: Abstract, Results (Copeman nodules: 91.7% of patients vs 8.3% of controls)
accuracy.population: 12 patients vs 12 healthy controls

name: Piriformis provocation maneuvers held for up to a minute (clinician): Freiberg, FAIR, heel-to-opposite-knee, Beatty
description: Each maneuver stretches or contracts the piriformis while the clinician watches for your usual buttock pain. They must be held for several tens of seconds. Compared against patients with L5/S1 disc-related root compression, the Beatty test was positive least often in disc patients.

accuracy.population: 250 piriformis cases (all positive; likely incorporation bias) vs 30 L5/S1 disc patients
vs 30 L5/S1 disc patients
vs 30 L5/S1 disc patients
vs 30 L5/S1 disc patients

name: Needle EMG of the leg muscles
description: Looks for signs of nerve damage in the leg muscles. These were found in most patients with L5/S1 disc-related root compression and in none with piriformis syndrome, so it helps tell the two apart.

accuracy.locator: Table 1 (neurogenic patterns 26/30 disc patients vs 0/250 piriformis)
accuracy.population: Root compression (L5/S1) vs piriformis syndrome

name: Standardized Evaluation of Pain (StEP): structured interview + bedside exam (clinician)
description: Six interview questions and ten bedside tests that separate nerve-root (radicular) pain from back pain without nerve involvement.

accuracy.population: 137 patients, radicular vs axial low back pain

name: Hip range-of-motion examination (clinician)
description: A clinician checks how far the hip moves compared with the other side. Normal inward movement (adduction) makes hip osteoarthritis much less likely.

accuracy.population: Hip/groin pain, reference = X-ray
Hip/groin pain, reference = X-ray

name: Hip X-ray
description: Shows joint narrowing and bone spurs. Bone spurs (osteophytes) best separated hip osteoarthritis from other causes of hip pain.

accuracy.population: 201 patients with hip pain vs other causes of hip pain

name: Sacroiliac provocation test cluster (clinician)
description: Six pain-provocation tests; three or more positive suggests the sacroiliac joint, and all six negative makes it unlikely.

accuracy.population: 48 LBP patients; reference = SIJ anaesthetic injection

name: Lateral hip clinical examination (palpation plus provocation tests)
description: A clinician presses on the outer hip and performs tendon-loading tests; MRI can confirm.

accuracy.population: 65 patients with lateral hip pain; reference = MRI

name: Ultrasound-guided posterior femoral cutaneous nerve block
description: An anaesthetic injection around the nerve, guided by high-resolution ultrasound; relief supports the diagnosis.

name: Ischiofemoral impingement test (clinician)
description: A clinician moves the hip into extension and adduction to see whether it reproduces the pain; MRI can show the narrowed space.

accuracy.population: 30 patients with posterior hip pain, spine excluded

name: Local anaesthetic obturator nerve block
description: An anaesthetic injection around the obturator nerve; relief of the exercise-related groin pain supports the diagnosis.

accuracy.population: 8 pooled studies, imaging or electrodiagnostic reference

name: Spurling's test (clinician)
description: The clinician tilts and extends your neck toward the painful side and presses down on your head; reproduction of your arm symptoms is positive. Highly specific, so a positive result supports a nerve root problem.

accuracy.population: Patients suspected of cervical radiculopathy

name: Upper limb neurodynamic tests, set of four (clinician)
description: The clinician moves your arm, wrist and neck in four set sequences that stretch the arm nerves. If all four are negative, a nerve root problem is unlikely.

accuracy.population: 12 studies of patients assessed for carpal tunnel syndrome

name: Nerve conduction studies and EMG (wrist)
description: Electrical tests of how fast and how well the median nerve conducts across the wrist.

accuracy.population: 12 studies of patients assessed for carpal tunnel syndrome

name: Ultrasound of the median nerve (wrist)
description: Measures the swelling of the median nerve at the carpal tunnel.

accuracy.population: 81 definite ulnar neuropathy at the elbow arms; asymptomatic controls

name: Nerve conduction studies across the elbow (short-segment)
description: Electrical tests of the ulnar nerve in short steps across the elbow, which locate the slowing more precisely than standard testing.

accuracy.population: 81 definite ulnar neuropathy at the elbow arms; asymptomatic controls

name: Ultrasound of the ulnar nerve (elbow)
description: Shows swelling of the ulnar nerve at the elbow; most useful when the nerve fibres themselves are damaged.

accuracy.locator: Abstract, Results (conduction to first dorsal interosseous including conduction block)
accuracy.population: 53 ulnar neuropathy at the wrist cases; specificity against controls

name: Ulnar motor conduction across the wrist
description: Electrical testing of the ulnar nerve branch to the hand muscles, recorded across the wrist to look for a conduction block.

accuracy.population: 41 surgically treated neurogenic TOS vs 19 healthy volunteers

name: Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve conduction
description: Electrical testing of the skin nerve of the inner forearm, which comes from the lowest part of the nerve bundle compressed in thoracic outlet syndrome.

accuracy.population: 34 patients (68 elbows) with lateral elbow pain; pilot

name: Neuromuscular ultrasound (radial nerve at the elbow)
description: Looks for compression of the radial nerve below the elbow and helps tell radial tunnel syndrome from tennis elbow. Pilot data only; the study abstract is internally inconsistent.

accuracy.population: 18 patients with suprascapular nerve entrapment (retrospective)

name: Shoulder MRI (muscle oedema)
description: MRI shows swelling (oedema) in the muscles the suprascapular nerve supplies, and where along the nerve the compression is.

accuracy.population: 20 patients with medial scapular winging vs 41 healthy subjects

name: Electrodiagnostic testing (serratus anterior)
description: Nerve conduction and EMG of the long thoracic nerve and the serratus anterior muscle.

accuracy.population: 53 patients, 70 affected nerves (no controls)

name: Nerve ultrasound (neuralgic amyotrophy)
description: High-resolution ultrasound of the affected nerves can show swelling, narrowing or twisting, and helps identify the few cases that need surgery.

accuracy.population: 20 anterior interosseous nerve syndrome patients vs 20 matched controls

name: MR neurography of the median nerve (upper arm)
description: High-resolution MRI of the median nerve, which shows the affected nerve fibres in the upper arm in anterior interosseous nerve syndrome.

name: Rotator cuff lag and strength tests (clinician)
description: The clinician places your arm in a position and checks whether you can hold it there (external and internal rotation lag tests); these were the most accurate findings for a full-thickness tear.

name: Forefoot ultrasound
description: Shows the thickened nerve between the long foot bones. The expert protocol rated it the most useful single step.

accuracy.population: Meta-analysis of 14 studies; surgery as reference standard

name: Forefoot MRI
description: An alternative to ultrasound for confirming a neuroma or showing another cause.

accuracy.population: Meta-analysis of 14 studies; surgery as reference standard

name: Mulder's click (clinician)
description: The clinician squeezes the forefoot from the sides with one hand while pressing a thumb into the sole at the suspected gap; a click that can be felt is positive. The studies disagree widely on its accuracy.

accuracy.population: 30 adults with forefoot pain (rearfoot and midfoot pain excluded), podiatry assessment, UK; 7 with a neuroma on ultrasound (Dando 2018)
22 people assessed before surgery, UK (16 neuromas at surgery)
40 people (54 neuromas) on ultrasound, UK; only 1 foot without a neuroma, so no specificity

name: Forefoot MRI (plantar plate)
description: Shows tears of the ligament under the small toe joints.

accuracy.population: Meta-analysis of 11 studies (227 plantar plates); intraoperative reference

name: Dynamic ultrasound (plantar plate)
description: Ultrasound while the toe is moved. More sensitive but less specific than MRI, so a negative scan helps rule a tear out.

accuracy.population: Meta-analysis of 11 studies (238 plantar plates); intraoperative reference

name: Drawer test of the 2nd toe joint (clinician)
description: The clinician checks the 2nd toe joint for instability (drawer sign).

accuracy.population: 90 patients (109 feet) who had plantar plate repair; intraoperative reference; retrospective

name: Stability test of the big toe joint (clinician)
description: The clinician holds the foot bone and moves the toe up and down (vertical Lachman or drawer test) and side to side; looseness compared with the other foot suggests a tear. Weakness bending the toe down against resistance also points to a tear.

name: Weight-bearing X-rays of both feet (big toe)
description: Usually normal, but a small flake of bone or sesamoids sitting further back than on the other foot (3 mm or more) points to a significant tear; a view with the toe bent up shows whether the sesamoids move with it.

name: MRI of the big toe joint
description: Commonly used in athletes and in moderate or severe injuries, to show tears of the tissue under the joint or damage to the joint surface.

name: Triple compression stress test (clinician)
description: With the ankle fully pointed down and the foot turned in, the clinician presses evenly over the tibial nerve behind the inner ankle; bringing on the symptoms is positive.

accuracy.population: 50 patients with suspected tarsal tunnel syndrome vs 40 healthy volunteers; electrodiagnostic reference (healthy controls, so specificity is likely overstated)

name: Ankle-brachial index (ABI)
description: Blood pressure is measured at the ankle and the arm with a cuff; an ankle pressure clearly lower than the arm pressure (ratio below 0.9) shows narrowed leg arteries.

recommendation.locator: Abstract, Introduction (Doppler ABI as the non-invasive gold standard)

accuracy.population: 20 studies, 1263 subjects; automated (oscillometric) ABI against Doppler ABI

name: Foot pulse check (clinician)
description: The clinician feels for the two pulses on the top and the inner ankle side of each foot; an absent pulse suggests narrowed arteries.

accuracy.locator: Abstract, Results (nurse, either pedal pulse absent)
accuracy.population: 315 legs of 158 mainly symptom-free primary-care patients at cardiovascular risk; Doppler ABI reference

name: Ultrasound of the peroneal nerve at the knee
description: High-resolution ultrasound of the nerve where it wraps around the fibular head, looking for swelling, a cyst or other compression.

accuracy.population: 40 patients with suspected common fibular neuropathy and 40 healthy controls (specificity likely overstated)

name: Nerve conduction studies and EMG (peroneal nerve, L5 muscles)
description: Electrical tests of conduction across the fibular head, with needle EMG of muscles that tell an L5 root or sciatic nerve problem apart from a peroneal nerve problem at the knee.

name: Lachman test (clinician)
description: With the knee slightly bent, the clinician pulls the shin forward on the thigh bone; extra movement or a soft end point suggests a torn ACL.

accuracy.population: 279 consecutive adults consulting for a new knee complaint (orthopaedic and family medicine clinics, Montreal); 43 partial or complete ACL tears vs the other knee disorders

name: Joint line tenderness and McMurray test (clinician)
description: The clinician presses along the joint line and bends and rotates the knee to provoke pain or a click from a torn meniscus.

accuracy.population: Review summary of primary studies
Review summary of primary studies

name: Examination for a swelling behind the knee (clinician), then ultrasound
description: The clinician feels behind the knee, straight and bent, for a smooth, soft swelling; ultrasound confirms a cyst.

accuracy.population: 10 studies, 542 patients (720 knees); mostly ultrasound reference; mixed populations including children and rheumatoid arthritis

name: Ottawa ankle rules (clinician), then X-ray
description: The clinician checks the four bone spots and whether you can take four steps; if any is positive, an X-ray shows whether a bone is broken.

accuracy.population: 15 studies, 8560 adults with acute ankle injuries

name: Calf-squeeze (Thompson) test and tendon examination (clinician)
description: With you lying face down, the clinician squeezes the calf (the foot should point down), feels for a gap in the tendon and checks its resting tension.

accuracy.population: 174 complete Achilles tears vs 28 suspected tears with an intact tendon

name: Achilles tendon palpation (clinician), then ultrasound
description: The clinician feels along the tendon for a tender or thickened area; ultrasound shows the tendon's structure.

accuracy.population: 2 small studies (Maffulli 2003, Hutchison 2013); ultrasound reference

name: Ankle anterior drawer test (clinician)
description: The clinician pulls the heel forward under the shin to test the main outer ankle ligament; extra movement points to a tear.

accuracy.population: Patients after an ankle sprain; imaging or surgical reference

name: DC/TMD examination (dentist or orofacial pain clinician)
description: The clinician measures jaw opening and presses on the jaw joint and chewing muscles to see whether this reproduces your familiar pain.

name: Occipital nerve block (clinician)
description: Local anaesthetic is injected next to the occipital nerve; if the pain eases for a while, the nerve is the source.

name: Diagnostic block of a neck joint or nerve (clinician)
description: Local anaesthetic is placed at a suspected neck joint or its nerve; if the headache goes away, the neck is the source.

name: Drawing fluid from the joint (joint aspiration)
description: A needle draws fluid from the swollen joint. A very high white cell count with mostly neutrophils points to infection, before the culture result is back; crystals in the fluid show gout.

name: Tests for the triggering infection (urine, swab or stool)
description: A urine test or swab for chlamydia, or a stool test for the gut bacteria (Campylobacter, Salmonella, Shigella, Yersinia), looks for the infection that set off the arthritis.

recommendation.locator: Laboratory Testing Confirmation of Triggering Infection

name: X-rays of both hips, front and frog-leg side views
description: Two views of the hips confirm and grade the slip; MRI can show the earliest changes when X-rays look normal.
